report_name: Settra Ransomware Claims Attack on Medical Firm MedEvolve

threat_actors.name: Settra
threat_actors.description: The Settra ransomware group claimed responsibility for a double extortion cyberattack against MedEvolve, a U.S. medical billing company. The group alleged the exfiltration of 820GB of sensitive data and posted the victim on its dark web leak site to pressure them into paying a ransom.
threat_actors.goals: Financial extortion through ransomware and data exfiltration.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: The Settra ransomware group engages in ransomware attacks, which involve encrypting victim data to disrupt operations and extort payment.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: As part of a double extortion tactic, the Settra group claimed to have exfiltrated 820GB of sensitive internal documents from MedEvolve before threatening to release it publicly.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit System Recovery
attack_patterns.description: The report suggests hunting for the use of `vssadmin` to delete volume shadow copies, a common ransomware technique to prevent system recovery.

attack_patterns.name: OS Credential Dumping
attack_patterns.description: The report suggests monitoring for credential dumping activity, such as tools targeting the lsass.exe process, which is a common precursor to ransomware deployment.

malware.name: Settra
malware.description: Settra is a ransomware family used by the eponymous group to conduct double extortion attacks, involving both data encryption and data exfiltration.

identities.name: MedEvolve
identities.description: A U.S.-based medical billing and practice management software company targeted by the Settra ransomware group.

infrastructure.name: Settra Leak Site
infrastructure.description: A dark web data leak site used by the Settra ransomware group to post victim information and threaten the release of exfiltrated data.

indicators.name: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
indicators.pattern:
title: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
id: 2b8a1e3c-7d4f-4b9a-8c6d-1e2f3a4b5c6d
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common technique used by ransomware to inhibit system recovery.
references:
  - https://www.dexpose.io/settra-ransomware-attack-on-medevolve/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-04
tags:
  - attack.t1490
  - attack.impact
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'delete'
      - 'shadows'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative activity, though rare in automated scripts.
level: high
indicators.description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common ransomware precursor technique mentioned as a hunting hint in the report.

indicators.name: LSASS Memory Access for Credential Dumping
indicators.pattern:
title: LSASS Memory Access for Credential Dumping
id: 9f8b7c6d-5e4f-4a3b-2c1d-0e9f8b7c6d5e
status: experimental
description: Detects processes accessing LSASS memory, which is often indicative of credential dumping attempts using tools like Mimikatz.
references:
  - https://www.dexpose.io/settra-ransomware-attack-on-medevolve/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-04
tags:
  - attack.t1003.001
  - attack.credential_access
logsource:
  category: process_access
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    GrantedAccess: '0x1010'
  filter_legit:
    SourceImage|endswith:
      - '\wmiprvse.exe'
      - '\svchost.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate security and system management tools.
level: high
indicators.description: Detects suspicious access to the LSASS process memory, a technique for credential dumping suggested as a hunting hint in the report.

relationships.source_name: LSASS Memory Access for Credential Dumping
